name: Ecopista da Maia
description: A short former railway corridor close to Porto, with a connection to Mandim metro.
note: The official page lists 3.1 km, but its downloadable GPS file contains only about 1.2 km. Only those supplied coordinates are drawn.

name: Ecopista de Famalicão
place: Póvoa de Varzim — Vila Nova de Famalicão
description: An old railway between the Atlantic coast and the countryside, with metro and railway connections at the two ends.

name: Ecopista de Guimarães
description: A former railway with an urban start in Guimarães and a more rural landscape towards Fafe.

name: Ecopista do Tâmega
place: Amarante — Celorico de Basto — Arco de Baúlhe
description: Follow the old Tâmega railway past stations, vineyards, bridges and views of the valley.

name: Ecopista do Corgo
description: A long inland railway trail through the Corgo valley, Vila Pouca de Aguiar and Pedras Salgadas.
note: The published route starts at Abambres. A ride beginning in Régua is a different, longer itinerary; it is not implied by this track.

name: Ecopista do Minho
description: The former Monção branch line beside the Minho, with vineyards, old stations and views towards Galicia.
note: 15 km is the IP Património railway section. Other visitor descriptions include longer riverside approaches and extensions.

name: Ecopista do Sabor
description: Two separate stretches of the former Sabor railway, from the Douro valley to the Mirandese plateau.
note: Two separate areas, not a continuous route. The supplied GPS file also contains discontinuities and a longer alignment than the 48 km described on the official page. Gaps are preserved.

name: Ecopista do Tua
description: Separate converted sections of the former Tua line across the inland northeast.
note: The official page describes 55.6 km in separate sections. Its GPS file contains about 41 km of drawn lines and does not cover every listed section. Do not assume a continuous connection.

name: Corredor Verde do Leça
description: A riverside green corridor through the Leça valley, passing the Lionesa area and historic bridges.
note: Drawn from OSM route members. The wider corridor is developed in phases; the line is not a claim that every planned extension is open.

name: Ciclovia da Foz
description: A seaside cycle path along the western edge of Porto. A convenient local starting point for an Atlantic outing.
note: Only the named OSM section is drawn; this does not trace the entire Porto marginal.

name: Ciclovia da Boavista
description: A local cycleway beside the western end of Avenida da Boavista, close to the coast and Parque da Cidade.
note: Named mapped sections only. There is no implication of a protected cycleway along the whole avenue.

name: Ciclovia da Ribeira da Granja
description: A green urban link through western Porto, useful for exploring the Pasteleira and riverfront area.

name: Matosinhos coastal cycleways
description: Named seaside cycleway sections north of Matosinhos, beside the Atlantic beaches.
note: Separate named sections are drawn. This is not a continuous Porto–Angeiras route.

name: Ciclovia Afurada — Aguda
place: Vila Nova de Gaia · Douro & oceanfront
description: A coastal cycle route from the fishing harbour at Afurada towards Aguda, beside the Douro and Gaia beaches.
source: Turismo do Porto e Norte · route guide
note: Location marker only; a verified line has not been included. The regional guide gives 14.35 km for Afurada–Aguda.

name: Ecovia litoral de Espinho
description: Mapped ecovia sections on the coast south of Espinho.
note: Named OSM sections only; walking and cycling rules can differ on nearby boardwalks.

name: Ecovia do Arda
description: An ecovia through the Arouca valley, alongside the river and agricultural land, with several access points.

name: Ecovia das Lagoas
description: Follow the Lima west from the medieval bridge towards the Bertiandos wetlands.

name: Ecovia da Laranja
place: Ponte de Lima — Refoios do Lima
description: The north-bank ecovia east of Ponte de Lima towards the Cais da Garrida.

name: Ecovia das Veigas
place: Ponte de Lima · south bank, westbound
description: A south-bank counterpart to the Lima ecovias, heading through the low fields west of the town.
source: Turismo de Ponte de Lima · visitor guide

name: Ecovia dos Açudes
place: Ponte de Lima — Ponte da Barca
description: A riverside route linking the two Lima valley towns, with weirs, picnic spots and gravel paths.

name: Ecovia do Vez
place: Jolda de São Paio — Arcos de Valdevez — Sistelo
description: Three stages alongside the Lima and Vez, ending in the terraced landscape around Sistelo.
source: Município de Arcos de Valdevez · route leaflet
note: The municipal leaflet prohibits bicycles from 1 July to 30 September. The upper stage is steeper and includes walking infrastructure. Check current signs and access rules.

name: Ecovia do Lima / Ermelo
description: An ecovia following the Lima upstream from the Ponte da Barca area towards Ermelo.
source: Município de Arcos de Valdevez · route leaflet

name: Caminho do Rio
place: Vila Nova de Cerveira · Rio Minho
description: The riverside ecopista through Cerveira, with the Castelinho park, river beaches and views across to Spain.
source: Município de Vila Nova de Cerveira
note: This card shows only OSM members within the Cerveira stretch. Neighbouring Minho routes have separate entries.

name: Ecovia do Atlântico
description: Atlantic-side paths through the Caminha coast, including the Sargaceiro and Camboas areas.

name: Ecovia Litoral Norte · Viana
place: Viana do Castelo · coast north of the Lima
description: Coastal ecovia sections between the Viana area and the beaches to the north.
note: Separate coastal sections are shown. This does not claim a continuous Caminha–Esposende route.

name: Ecovia Litoral Norte · Esposende
description: Coastal ecovia sections around Esposende and the Parque Natural do Litoral Norte.
note: The official page describes gaps between sections, including the Cávado crossing and links north towards Foz do Neiva. Keep these separate when planning a trip.

name: Ecovia do Cávado e do Homem
description: A riverbank outing between the Faial area in Prado and the Mirante leisure area in Soutelo.
note: This entry covers named mapped sections in Vila Verde, not the full regional network planned between the coast and Gerês.

name: Ecovia do Rio Este
description: The mapped river corridor through Braga, useful for a short urban walk or ride beside the Este.
note: OSM mapped sections only. Extensions towards Famalicão are not inferred.

name: Ecovia do Ave
description: A mapped riverside route on the Ave in the Trofa area.
note: This is the Trofa-area route, not the separately proposed Vila do Conde project.

name: Ecovia do Rio Homem
description: A short riverside walking route and boardwalk by Moimenta, at the edge of the Gerês area.
note: Location marker only. This is separate from the Vila Verde Cávado–Homem route.

name: Ecovia do Rabaçal
description: Three marked walking routes converging on the Rabaçal river beach, through river valleys and villages.
note: Three different routes form a network. The name “ecovia” does not make every section suitable for a casual bicycle ride.

name: Ecovia do Tâmega · Chaves — Verín
description: A cross-border river corridor extending north of Chaves into Galicia.
note: OSM route members only. This entry intentionally includes the Spanish continuation beyond Norte.

name: Ecopista do Vouga
place: Sernada do Vouga — Sever do Vouga — Viseu
description: A long former railway through the Vouga valley, with old stations, tunnels and the stone arches of the Poço de Santiago bridge.
note: This is the wider Sernada–Viseu route published by IP Património. The Viseu Dão Lafões visitor site describes a shorter, roughly 65 km section; the different lengths refer to different extents.

name: Ecopista do Dão
description: The old Dão railway follows the Dão and Pavia valleys through vineyards, woodland, tunnels and former stations.

name: Ecovia do Mondego
place: Santa Comba Dão — Aguieira — Penacova / Caneiro
description: A river-and-reservoir itinerary following the Mondego, with both road and off-road sections.
source: CIM Região de Coimbra · Ecovia do Mondego
note: Official access notice checked 24 October 2026: several sections are impassable, with unstable slopes, missing barriers, landslides and submerged paths. Confirm conditions with the route operator before visiting. The mapped line is a route reference, not confirmation that it is open.

name: Ecopista do Ramal do Lena
description: A former mining railway in the Serra dos Candeeiros landscape, also known as the Ecopista da Bezerra.
note: Only the mapped railway trail is drawn. The municipal 12 km circular walking itinerary includes additional paths and is not the same as this linear ecopista.

name: Ecovia da Guarda
description: An urban walking and cycling corridor beside the VICEG, connecting neighbourhoods and the Rio Diz park area.
note: Only named OSM sections are drawn. The published 9 km describes the wider corridor and is longer than the included geometry.

name: Ecopista da Várzea da Rainha
description: A rural path through the Arnóia floodplain and orchards towards the Óbidos lagoon.
note: OSM includes branches and lagoon-side sections. Drawn distance describes the included network, not a single recommended itinerary.

name: Ecovia das Águas
description: A mapped mountain-bike itinerary between the Óbidos area and its rural water landscape.
note: The OSM route is tagged for mountain biking. Do not assume smooth surfaces or a cycleway separated from traffic.

name: Ecopista / Pista Ciclopedonal de Mira
place: Mira · Praia de Mira · lagoons & woodland
description: A municipal network through lagoons, beaches, dunes and pinewoods, also known as the Ecopista de Mira.
note: Location marker only; no complete verified network trace is included. Municipal publications give different totals as the network expands, so no single route length is shown.

name: BioRia · Percurso de Salreu
description: A nature loop through wetlands, rice fields and saltmarsh, starting by the BioRia environmental interpretation centre.
note: This entry traces the Salreu route only. BioRia has several other connected nature routes around Estarreja.

name: Ciclovia da Estrada Atlântica
place: Mata do Urso — Pedrógão — Vieira — São Pedro de Moel — Nazaré
description: A coastal cycling corridor through pinewoods and seaside towns in the central Atlantic region.
note: The line follows OSM members of the northern coastal corridor. The Foz do Arelho–Salir do Porto section has a separate map entry. Connecting roads and surface conditions vary.

name: Percurso Polis · Rio Lis
place: Leiria · São Romão — city riverfront — Barosa area
description: An urban riverside corridor for walking, running and cycling along the Lis.
note: Only named OSM sections are drawn; these do not cover the full 5.4 km municipal route.

name: Ecopista de Almeida
description: A short path around the outside of Almeida’s star-shaped fortress, described in the Centro de Portugal visitor guide.
source: Turismo Centro de Portugal · visitor feature
note: Approximate location marker near the fortress; no verified perimeter trace is included. This ecopista is not a converted railway.

name: Passadiços do Mondego
description: A walking itinerary beside the upper Mondego and its tributaries, combining wooden walkways, bridges and older paths.
note: A walking route with many steps and around 600 m of accumulated ascent, rather than a casual cycle trail. Check tickets, opening arrangements and any access notices on the official website.
activity: Walking only · stairs and steep sections

name: Ecovia Fátima — Ortiga
place: Fátima parish church — Santuário da Ortiga
description: A walking and cycling link from the old parish of Fátima towards the Ortiga sanctuary.

name: Ciclovia Foz do Arelho — Salir do Porto
description: A coastal cycle lane along the Estrada Atlântica between Foz do Arelho and Salir do Porto.
note: The municipality describes a painted cycling lane alongside the road; it is not physically separated from motor traffic throughout.

name: Ciclovia do Mondego · lower valley
description: Named mapped cycling sections along the lower Mondego valley, separate from the Ecovia do Mondego upstream.
note: Only named OSM sections in the lower valley are drawn. No continuous Coimbra–Figueira connection or current opening status is inferred.

name: Passadiços do Rio Uíma
place: Santa Maria da Feira · Fiães / Lobão
description: Wooden boardwalks and riverside paths through the Parque das Ribeiras do Uíma, with wetland woodland and places to observe wildlife.
source: Município de Santa Maria da Feira
note: The municipal park brochure prohibits bicycles (velocípedes), so this entry is marked for walking. The published 2 km refers to the Fiães–Lobão park. The wider Uíma corridor and extensions towards Caldas de São Jorge, Pigeiros and Escapães are separate; their completion is not implied by this line. Follow current signs at the site.
activity: Walking · bicycles prohibited in park brochure
